strengths: Identifies and formally defines a genuine practical problem in LLM-driven compression (prediction mismatch due to GPU non-determinism) that has not been explicitly addressed before
Clean theoretical framework with rigorous correctness proof (Theorem 1) and compression loss analysis deriving O(√(δ log(1/δ))) bounds
Well-designed algorithm that is model-agnostic, intuitive (bin-based quantization with helper bits), and works as a drop-in replacement for arithmetic coding
Elegant connection between L∞ logit bounds and total variation distance (Proposition 1) that motivates the bounded mismatch setting
Experimental validation successfully demonstrates correct decoding and achieves compression significantly better than gzip (7% vs 41% on enwik8)
weaknesses: Critical gap between theory and practice: All experiments use synthetic IID uniform noise to logits, but authors explicitly acknowledge (Section 6) that real-world LLM non-determinism remains unvalidated. Real GPU non-determinism patterns may differ fundamentally from synthetic injection
Incomplete practical evaluation: No measurement of computational overhead, memory costs, or wall-clock time compared to standard arithmetic coding, limiting deployment feasibility assessment
Very limited experimental scope: Single model (Llama 3.1 8B), single domain (Wikipedia text), only two parameter settings with no sensitivity analysis or ablation studies
Rolling context window design choice (reset every 256 tokens) lacks justification and is likely to impact compression significantly, but is not analyzed or ablated

Theory assumes encoder probabilities equal true distribution (Section 4.2), which is unrealistic for finite-data trained LLMs; uniform bin distribution assumption (footnote 3) acknowledged but not empirically validated
Modest algorithmic novelty: Once prediction mismatch is identified, applying quantization is a straightforward solution; limited innovation beyond problem formulation
No characterization of real-world mismatch magnitudes: What are typical ||u−v||∞ values in actual GPU computations? Without this, practitioners cannot determine appropriate δ values

Missing ablations and comparisons: No sensitivity to noise distribution type (Gaussian vs uniform), no comparison to alternative robust coding approaches, no comparison to simpler quantization baselines
Reproducibility concerns: No code availability mentioned, arithmetic coding implementation dependencies not specified, quantized model loading details sparse

strengths: Addresses a genuine and timely practical problem in model-driven compression: prediction mismatch from non-determinism in neural network inference
Rigorous theoretical framework with sound proofs (Theorem 1, Proposition 1) and meaningful compression overhead bounds O(√δ log(1/δ))
Model-agnostic algorithm design serving as drop-in replacement for arithmetic coding
Comprehensive experimental validation across multiple models (3 architectures), datasets (6+ diverse sources including non-English), and both synthetic and real non-determinism
Significant compression improvements over traditional methods (0.078 vs 0.46 for gzip) despite robustness overhead
Clear presentation with good motivation, algorithm description, and illustrative examples
Honest reporting of assumptions that don't hold in practice and identification of improvement opportunities
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: core quantization + helper bits approach is relatively straightforward; concurrent work (Hu & Tang 2026) pursues similar ideas, suggesting approach isn't unique

Significant theory-practice gap: uniformity assumption for next-bit probability distribution (Section 4.2) severely violated in practice—Table 2 shows measured helper bit probability 5-6× lower than theoretical expectation, yet algorithm still uses assumed probability for encoding

Suboptimal algorithm implementation: Table 2 clearly shows inefficiency in helper bit encoding that could substantially reduce overhead, acknowledged only as future work rather than addressed in current implementation
Substantial compression overhead: 6-22% at δ=10⁻⁵, scaling to 200-300% at δ=10⁻². Limited guidance on choosing δ for practical applications

Limited real non-determinism evaluation: tested only on Llama 3.1 across two Apple laptops (M2 Pro vs M4 Max) with small test set (100 articles + 250KB). Figure 3 shows non-uniform logit differences, challenging bounded mismatch model assumptions

Insufficient comparison with related work: concurrent Hu & Tang (2026) mentioned but not compared; no comparison with deterministic backend solutions (He & Lab 2025, Yuan et al. 2025); limited discussion of when PMATIC preferred over alternatives
Missing ablation studies: no analysis of bin size selection, alphabet size effects, or rolling context window impact; no ablation on design choices
Presentation issues: Figure 1 appears twice (pages 5-6, apparent formatting error); dense notation (S^j_{i,b}); limited analysis of overhead from longform bitstring representation

strengths: Identifies and formalizes a novel, well-motivated problem: prediction mismatch in model-driven compression due to neural network non-determinism, with clear practical relevance as LLMs are deployed across heterogeneous systems

Solid theoretical contributions with rigorous proofs: Theorem 1 guarantees correctness under bounded conditional TV distance; Proposition 1 elegantly bounds CTV distance via logit bounds; compression loss analysis provides O(√δ log(1/δ)) bounds

Clever, model-agnostic algorithm design: the helper bit mechanism enables encoder-decoder synchronization elegantly; quantization with δ-interiors is intuitive and practical; works as drop-in replacement for arithmetic coding

Comprehensive experimental validation: multiple models (LLaMA, Mistral, Qwen) with diverse vocabulary sizes; multilingual datasets (English, French, Chinese); outperforms standard compressors (gzip, brotli, xz) even with robustness overhead; includes both synthetic and real non-determinism testing
Empirically validates problem existence with real hardware: Figure 3 demonstrates actual logit differences across Apple M2/M4 chipsets; demonstrates PMATIC solves the problem in practice with δ=0.01

Well-written with clear presentation: good motivation, formal problem statement, intuitive figures (especially Figure 2's encoding example), thorough appendix with implementation details and additional analysis
weaknesses: Theoretical assumptions in compression loss analysis are strong and unrealistic: assumes encoder probabilities equal true distribution (ignoring model error); assumes uniform probability distribution within bins (violated when probabilities cluster near 0, 1, or boundaries); acknowledged as 'worst-case non-adversarial' but limits practical guarantees

Real non-determinism validation is limited in scope: tested only between two specific Apple devices (M2 Pro to M4 Max) on small datasets (100 articles, 250KB Emma split into 5KB files); no cross-vendor GPU testing (NVIDIA, AMD) or framework variation testing (PyTorch versions, CUDA versions); δ=0.01 estimated empirically without systematic characterization

Helper bit efficiency gap unresolved: actual helper-1 frequency significantly underestimates theoretical prediction (Table 2: 0.00051 vs 0.002 expected for δ=10^-5), indicating algorithm is suboptimally tuned; paper acknowledges better probability estimation could yield 'significant improvement' but doesn't explore this

Limited experimental scope: only text compression validated; images/vision/audio mentioned as future work but not tested; applicability to other domains remains speculative; rolling context window (512 tokens, reset every 256) introduced for speed but impact on results unclear

Incomplete ablation studies: bin radius selection (Eq. 20) tested at only three δ values with fixed r values; no systematic exploration of r vs compression tradeoff; no investigation of design parameter sensitivity
No fundamental information-theoretic limits established: paper doesn't characterize whether O(√δ log(1/δ)) overhead is optimal or if better bounds exist; gap between theory and practice not explained
Limited engagement with concurrent work: Hu & Tang (2026) mentioned but not compared experimentally or methodologically; unclear how PMATIC differs in approach or relative merits

Presentation issues: Figure 1 appears twice (pages 5-6) with different contexts causing confusion; notation S^{b_{j-1}_i} used before intuitive introduction; 'longform' concept central to algorithm but could be explained earlier
